approachQuestion.prompt:
Rising readings

An array a contains recorded integer readings. You may increase any entry by one per operation and may never decrease it. Return the minimum total operations needed to make the readings strictly increasing while preserving their positions.

Example 1: a=[3,3,1] → 5, by producing [3,4,5].
Example 2: a=[-2,0,4] → 0.
Example 3: a=[] → 0.

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; -10^9 ≤ a[i] ≤ 10^9. Input is read-only. Return only the stated scalar result. All arithmetic and comparisons use constant-time exact 64-bit operations; all intermediate values fit.

options.text: Keep the previous adjusted value. For each next entry x choose max(x,previous+1), add its increase to the total, and update previous. Leave the first entry unchanged; return zero for an empty array.
options.feedback: The first reading never benefits from an increase. At every later position the chosen value is the smallest feasible one; choosing a larger value spends more now and cannot reduce any later requirement.

options.text: Whenever a[i] ≤ a[i-1], add a[i-1]+1-a[i] using only the original neighboring values, and sum these amounts.
options.feedback: A previous entry may itself have been increased. For [2,2,2], this counts 2 rather than the required 3 for [2,3,4].

options.text: Sort a copy and count the increments needed to separate equal values.
options.feedback: Sorting changes the required positions. For [3,1], sorting would need no increase, but preserving positions requires raising 1 to 4 at cost 3.

options.text: Enumerate every legal sequence of decisions, evaluate each complete candidate, and return the best result.
options.feedback: Exhaustive search can find the right result, but revisits combinations of decisions that the safe local rule resolves directly. The number of candidates grows far beyond what the input limit permits.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed frontier method, regardless of your previous choice. Use exactly the frontier method above as iterative scans with scalar indices, counters and accumulators. Do not copy the input and do not store a decision list. Let n be the number of input records or positions. Choose the tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Input and returned scalar are excluded. All other live storage, including copying and any call stack, is counted. No hashing or expected-time operations are used.

feedback.reason: One pass updates a previous adjusted value and total increase.

messages.text: The method stores no per-item history or copied input.
The scans do not restart for each item.
In the worst case every input item can affect the answer.

details: Each reading is compared once with previous+1 and causes one increase update. Thus all n entries take O(n) work. previous and the total replace an n-entry adjusted copy, giving O(1) auxiliary space.
“Time O(n), auxiliary space O(n)”: The method stores no per-item history or copied input.
“Time O(n²), auxiliary space O(1)”: The scans do not restart for each item.
“Time O(1), auxiliary space O(1)”: In the worst case every input item can affect the answer.
